'''Coats:''' {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} {{legend0|#d72f30|70–80%}}
'''Hill:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Dan Coats]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Dan Coats]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Indiana}} The '''1990 United States Senate special election in Indiana''' was a [[By-election|special election]] held on November 6, 1990, in order to fill Indiana's [[Classes of United States senators|Class III]] Senate seat in the [[United States Senate]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Senator [[Dan Coats]], who was appointed to replace [[Dan Quayle]] two years prior, was challenged by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee [[Baron Hill (politician)|Baron Hill]], a [[Indiana House of Representatives|state representative]] from [[Seymour, Indiana]] won the election to serve out the remainder of the term. ==Background == In 1986, incumbent Senator [[Dan Quayle]] sought reelection facing Democratic challenger [[Jill Long]] and was reelected in a landslide.{{Cite news |date=December 30, 1986 |title=Did 1986 election show a trend or just confusion? |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/551474728/ |access-date=September 23, 2025 |work=[[The Reporter-Times]] |page=10 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[United Press International]]}} During the [[1988 United States presidential election|1988 presidential election]], [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee [[George H. W. Bush]] selected Quayle as his running mate.{{Cite news |last=Margolis |first=Jon |date=August 18, 1988 |title=Why Bush Cast Aside VP Tradition |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1988/08/18/why-bush-cast-aside-vp-tradition/ |access-date=September 23, 2025 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]]}} The Bush-Quayle ticket defeated the [[Michael Dukakis|Dukakis]]-[[Lloyd Bentsen|Bentsen]] ticket in the general election by a 53% to 46% margin, capturing 40 states and 426 [[Electoral College (United States)|electoral votes]].{{Cite web |last=Liep |first=Dave |title=1988 Presidential General Election Results |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/national.php?year=1988&minper=0&off=0&elect=0 |access-date=September 23, 2025 |website=[[Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections]]}} After being elected, Quayle resigned from the Senate. Indiana Governor [[Robert D. Orr]] appointed Representative [[Dan Coats]] of [[Indiana's 4th congressional district]] to fill the vacancy.{{Cite news |date=December 13, 1988 |title=State Demos cautiously eye '90 Senate race |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/106156685/ |access-date=September 23, 2025 |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |page=14 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} The 1990 election was held as part of the [[United States midterm election|midterm election cycle]] of Republican President [[George H. W. Bush]]'s term.{{Cite news |last1=Dewar |first1=Helen |last2=Yang |first2=John E. |date=November 6, 1990 |title=The Senate Incumbents Win Control Remains with Democrats |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1990/11/07/the-senate/88a317b4-abae-4a7c-9a3c-f65fe6b52b54/ |access-date=March 12, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}} Historically, the President's party struggles during the midterms.{{Cite news |last=Elving |first=Ron |date=November 13, 2022 |title=The midterms didn't produce a wave. Here's what that's meant historically |url=https://www.npr.org/2022/11/13/1136103595/the-midterms-didnt-produce-a-wave-heres-what-thats-meant-historically |access-date=April 1, 2025 |work=[[NPR]] |language=en}} ==Primaries == * [[Baron Hill (politician)|Baron Hill]] ([[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]]), State Representative{{Cite news |last=Richardson |first=Doug |date=May 8, 2025 |title=Voters return after 18-month absence |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/252310751/ |access-date=October 9, 2025 |work=[[The Star Press]] |page=17 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} * [[Dan Coats]] ([[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]]), incumbent U.S. Senator Coats and Hill both won their respective party's nomination unopposed. ==General election == Coats used television commercials that raised questions about Hill's consistency in opposing new taxes, and Hill gained notoriety for walking the length of the state to meet voters. === Results === The election was held on November 6, 1990.{{Cite news |date=November 7, 1990 |title=McWherter, Gore coast to victories |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/963927131/ |access-date=September 23, 2025 |work=[[Bristol Herald Courier]] |pages=1, 8 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}{{Cite news |last=Espo |first=David |date=November 7, 1990 |title=Demos win Texas, Florida, four other Governships; Helms wins |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/344952161/ |access-date=September 23, 2025 |work=[[The Times and Democrat]] |pages=1, 4 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Coats, like most incumbents in the [[1990 United States Senate elections]],{{Cite news |last1=Dewar |first1=Helen |last2=Yang |first2=John E. |date=November 6, 1990 |title=The Senate Incumbents Win Control Remains with Democrats |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1990/11/07/the-senate/88a317b4-abae-4a7c-9a3c-f65fe6b52b54/ |access-date=September 23, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}} was able to hold his seat, winning the remainder of Quayle's term.{{Cite news |last=O'Neill |first=John R. |date=November 5, 1990 |title=Old political foes back home to fight for party |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/105987624/ |access-date=September 23, 2025 |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |page=26 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}{{Cite news |date=November 7, 1990 |title=At a glance On January 3, 1991, Coats was sworn in to the [[102nd United States Congress]] by then–Vice President Quayle alongside his fellow Senator-elect.{{Cite video |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/senate-highlight/swearing-in-of-senate-members/10810 |title=Swearing-In of Senate Members |date=January 3, 1991 |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=5:27}} In the [[1992 United States Senate election in Indiana]], Coats was elected for a full term.{{Cite web |last=Leip |first=Dave |title=1992 Senatorial General Election Results - Indiana
